proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof: J₂(r) → 0 from the zero upper density of |ϑ|Hⁿ⌞(A ∖ C_i) at x (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), with Ch. 1, Thm 3.6). It is stated on the original side of the blow-up. By the change of variables, (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_S f(η_r(z))ϑ(z) dHⁿ(z) is the parent's J₂(r) when S = A ∖ C_i, but this child neither needs nor uses that identity.

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η_r := blowUpMap x r, so η_r(z) = r⁻¹(z − x); B_ρ(p) := closedBall p ρ; μ' := (Hⁿ⌞A).withDensity(‖ϑ‖ₑ); φ(ρ) := (ρⁿ)⁻¹·μ'.real(S ∩ B_ρ(x)). The hypothesis says φ(ρ) → 0 as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ).

1. Bounds for f. f is continuous with compact support, so there is M with |f(y)| ≤ M for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). The topological support tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) for some R₀ (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0. If y ∉ B_R(0), then y ∉ tsupport f, hence f(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).

2. Weighted measure of subsets of A. Let T be Borel with T ⊆ A. Then:
- μ'(T) = ∫⁻_T ‖ϑ‖ₑ d(Hⁿ⌞A) (withDensity_apply, T Borel);
- this equals ∫⁻ ‖ϑ‖ₑ d(Hⁿ⌞(T ∩ A)) (Measure.restrict_restrict, T Borel);
- this equals ∫⁻_T ‖ϑ‖ₑ dHⁿ, since T ∩ A = T.
Since ϑ is integrable on A ⊇ T, it is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞T, so ∫_T |ϑ| dHⁿ = (∫⁻_T ‖ϑ‖ₑ dHⁿ).toReal (integral_norm_eq_lintegral_enorm). Hence μ'.real(T) = ∫_T |ϑ| dHⁿ.

3. Pointwise bound. Fix r > 0 and put B := B_{rR}(x), a Borel set. For every z: |f(η_r(z))·ϑ(z)| ≤ M·1_B(z)·|ϑ(z)|.
- If z ∈ B, this is |f(η_r(z))| ≤ M multiplied by |ϑ(z)|.
- If z ∉ B, then ‖z − x‖ > rR, so ‖η_r(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ > R (norm_smul, r > 0). Hence f(η_r(z)) = 0 by step 1, and both sides are 0.

4. Integral bound. The function z ↦ M·1_B(z)·|ϑ(z)| is integrable on S: |ϑ| is integrable on S ⊆ A, multiplying by the indicator of the Borel set B preserves integrability (Integrable.indicator), and so does the constant factor M. By norm_integral_le_of_norm_le (which needs no integrability of the integrand) and step 3:
|∫_S f(η_r(z))ϑ(z) dHⁿ(z)| ≤ ∫_S M·1_B|ϑ| dHⁿ
= M·∫_{S∩B} |ϑ| dHⁿ (integral_const_mul, integral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict)
= M·μ'.real(S ∩ B) (step 2 with T := S ∩ B, which is Borel and ⊆ A).

5. Rescaling. Since (rR)ⁿ = rⁿRⁿ and Rⁿ > 0, (rⁿ)⁻¹ = Rⁿ·((rR)ⁿ)⁻¹. Hence, for every r > 0:
|(rⁿ)⁻¹∫_S f(η_r(z))ϑ(z) dHⁿ(z)| ≤ (rⁿ)⁻¹·M·μ'.real(S ∩ B_{rR}(x)) = M·Rⁿ·φ(rR).

6. Limit. The map r ↦ rR tends to 0 as r → 0 (continuity) and is positive for r > 0, so it maps 𝓝[>] 0 into 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within). Composing with the hypothesis, φ(rR) → 0, hence M·Rⁿ·φ(rR) → M·Rⁿ·0 = 0 as r → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0 (Tendsto.const_mul). Step 5 holds for all r > 0, in particular eventually in 𝓝[>] 0. By squeeze_zero_norm', (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_S f(η_r(z))ϑ(z) dHⁿ(z) → 0. ∎
